nodes.label: Sudoku Arena Gameplay Assets
nodes.rationale: Board tiles, interaction states, pencil-note props, difficulty seals, sealed puzzle envelope, solved badge and reward trophy were generated with OpenAI image generation specifically for Neo MiniApps, then cropped/composed locally, so they are original project assets rather than third-party game media.

nodes.label: generate-art.mjs Deterministic Art Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Runtime WebP/AVIF/PNG variants and transparent per-object textures are regenerated deterministically by prebuild so a clean checkout fails loudly instead of silently depending on stale checked-in outputs.

nodes.label: generate-audio.mjs PCM Audio Synthesis
nodes.rationale: Twelve interaction cues and three ambient loops are synthesized as original PCM WAV files so no third-party or commercial-game recording enters the bundle.

nodes.label: verify-assets.mjs Release Asset Gate
nodes.rationale: Checks expected dimensions for 186 public images, requires alpha on all 162 per-object textures, validates every PCM WAV header/duration, and rejects a package/manifest version mismatch.

nodes.label: model-kit surface() Procedural Skin Pass
nodes.rationale: Each finish (produce, glaze, ceramic, metal, wood, fabric, paper, matte) gets a shared 64x64 procedural albedo/normal/roughness triple so material response comes from code rather than painted identity symbols or per-instance texture downloads.

nodes.label: 162 Gameplay Match Identities
nodes.rationale: Documentation deliberately distinguishes 162 gameplay identities from the 54 authored model/icon bases so the project never claims 162 unrelated source models.

nodes.label: Same-Silhouette Near-Match Colourway System
nodes.rationale: Variants reuse an authored base with a separate material colour, localized name, physics identity, size tier and deterministic hue treatment, keeping colourways distinguishable without painting symbols onto objects; the thumbnail generator segments the dominant body material so structural accents survive recolouring.

nodes.label: Genre-Mechanics Review Boundary
nodes.rationale: Gameplay rules may resemble a known three-match extraction genre, but brand marks, commercial character designs, commercial source code and commercial media are declared outside the project source set.

nodes.label: art-src SOURCE_MANIFEST SHA-256 Pin
nodes.rationale: ImageGen job IDs and verbatim prompts were never emitted into the workspace, so the immutable SHA-256 list is declared the canonical identity record instead of inventing unverifiable provenance.

nodes.label: Original Chibi Goose Art Direction
nodes.rationale: Three independent settings (fresh market, farm kitchen, night market), warm toy-like material language and portrait mobile backdrops, with no original-game brand marks or character copies.

nodes.label: Goose Basket Shuffle Production Readiness
nodes.rationale: Separates repository/browser automation from evidence only real iOS/Android hardware can produce; a green local build is necessary but explicitly not sufficient for mobile release approval, so the decision stays CONDITIONAL RELEASE CANDIDATE.

nodes.label: verify:release Local Release Gate
nodes.rationale: One authoritative command chains tests, ESLint, shim hygiene, balance audit, release audit, dependency audit, deterministic asset regeneration, asset gate, TypeScript, Vite build, bundle scan, gzip budgets, dist digest, dist staging and staged host parity so a release cannot be staged from a dirty or partially generated public/ tree.

nodes.label: Real-Device Release Gate
nodes.rationale: iOS motion permission, Android motion delivery, toss calibration, audio unlock/mix, haptics, frame time, memory/GPU stability, background/resume, responsive input and full three-theme flow must each be recorded on at least one current iPhone and one mid-range Android before unconditional release.

nodes.label: build:device-qa Instrumented Build
nodes.rationale: Rejects missing, placeholder or non-hex VITE_BUILD_SHA so a physical-device run cannot produce 'local-unbound' evidence, and regenerates the deterministic art/audio bank so evidence cannot come from a stale resource set.

nodes.label: device-qa:verify-suite Evidence Verifier
nodes.rationale: Runs every report with --strict-evidence-files and requires at least one accepted iOS/Safari and one accepted Android/Chrome report for the same app version and build id; the single-report verifier is only a precheck.

nodes.label: Staged Host Parity Gate
nodes.rationale: The host-served platform/host-app/public/miniapps/zhuada-e tree is replaced from the current dist/ and must match file-for-file and SHA-256-for-SHA-256, so the framing host cannot serve a drifted bundle.

nodes.label: Gzip Bundle Budget Gate
nodes.rationale: Three.js and cannon-es are split into cacheable chunks and gzip budgets cover the entry, scene, Three.js and physics chunks so CDN bundle delivery stays bounded.

nodes.label: Production Bundle Leak Scan
nodes.rationale: Rejects leaked Device QA instrumentation or playtest debug shortcuts from the production runtime while requiring them in the dist-device-qa artifact.

nodes.label: No Offline Support Policy
nodes.rationale: neo-manifest.json declares features.offlineSupport:false; there is no app-owned Service Worker or precache manifest, so incidental browser caching must not be advertised as offline support.

nodes.label: Chain-Free Local Run Policy
nodes.rationale: Level generation, physics, matching, scoring, progress and resumable-run snapshots need no chain or API; this release ships no wallet, leaderboard fetch or score submission and the drawer reports only a device-local personal record.

nodes.label: Memory/GPU Stability Evidence Contract
nodes.rationale: Requires >=20 start/retry/exit/resume cycles, one long Level 15 run, a memory timeline path, memoryTrend=flat, restartSlowdown=none and contextLossLoop=false.

nodes.label: Frame-Time Smoothness Gate
nodes.rationale: Median FPS >=55, P95 frame time <=25ms, longest foreground frame <=80ms, long-frame rate <=0.6% and worst consecutive slow-frame burst <=2 frames, because an acceptable median FPS alone hides visible hitching.

nodes.label: 24-Level Monte-Carlo Balance Audit
nodes.rationale: scripts/tune.mjs parses the level curve and mathematical triple invariants from source and audits them before release.

nodes.label: Goose Basket Shuffle Mini-Game
nodes.rationale: Production mini-game built with React, Three.js and cannon-es using an original three-match extraction rule set, three selectable art themes, local progress, optional timed play, generated sound effects and an opt-in motion pan-toss gesture.

nodes.label: Streamed Bottom Reservoir (54 to 18+27)
nodes.rationale: 18-1,584 logical items back a run while the live Cannon body ceiling stays at 54; complete-triple layers emerge from under the pile after visible excavation instead of falling from the top, which matches the reference video's near-empty-then-whole-layer rhythm.

nodes.label: Constrained Render Tier
nodes.rationale: Software renderers and low-memory four-core phones reduce antialias/shadow/raster cost without removing items, physics bodies, collisions, materials, picking, refill waves or game rules.

nodes.label: Opt-in Phone Motion Pan-Toss Gesture
nodes.rationale: Motion stays disabled until the player presses a visible Enable button, and a visible Shake button remains available when sensor access is unsupported, blocked, denied or cooling down.

nodes.label: In-Memory Motion Sample Privacy Rule
nodes.rationale: Motion samples are processed in memory inside the current page and are never persisted or uploaded.

nodes.label: Seven-Slot Tray Matching Rule
nodes.rationale: Fixed seven slots filled left to right, three-of-a-kind clears, a full tray loses; holes compact left and same-kind items group together.

nodes.label: 24-Level Curve (18-1,584 Items)
nodes.rationale: L1 randomly selects a balanced three-kind tutorial; L2 jumps immediately to 48 scene kinds and 864 logical items, with size-family and exact-silhouette guardrails keeping replays varied without a fixed opening layout.

nodes.label: Reference Implementation Compliance Record
nodes.rationale: The product goal is a close playable genre implementation, not a copy of the commercial game or an unlicensed community repository.

nodes.label: Juejin Reference Article
nodes.rationale: The fetch reached a wait/interstitial page so no source text was imported; treated as a named public learning reference only.

nodes.label: CSDN CC BY-SA Reference Article
nodes.rationale: Marked CC 4.0 BY-SA and describes a Three.js + Cannon.js loop; only uncopyrightable gameplay ideas and architecture comparison may be used, never the Vue source, textures, screenshots or prose.

nodes.label: Gitee hanshuoggg/big-goose Repository
nodes.rationale: Excluded from production reuse because the reviewed repository page does not specify a license.

nodes.label: Commercial WeChat Zhua-Da-E Game
nodes.rationale: Proprietary with no known open-source release; art, sound, logo, brand presentation, package assets and source code must not be extracted or reproduced.

nodes.label: Allowed Genre-Mechanics Reuse
nodes.rationale: Reusable: physically simulated 3D objects in an open container, item extraction, seven-slot collection, three-of-kind clearing, tray-full failure, refill streaming, shake/toss interaction, and the Three.js + rigid-body + raycast-picking architecture.

nodes.label: Reference Port Release Rule
nodes.rationale: Any future iteration that copies or ports code/assets must update this file with the precise source URL and commit/date, add license text and attribution, and rerun the release gate.

nodes.label: Reference Video Audit Baseline
nodes.rationale: A 136.6s 308x720 clip sampled at 15 timestamps is used strictly to extract pacing, spatial proportion and interaction-feedback baselines, never original art, copy, advertising, characters or commercial marks.

nodes.label: Reference UI Composition Metrics
nodes.rationale: Container occupies ~95-98% of screen width, HUD ~200px, tray/tools ~130px, fixed 7 tray cells about 40x42px each, so core play always completes within one screen.

nodes.label: Refactor Acceptance Matrix
nodes.rationale: Each row separates the video-visible baseline from the engineering threshold, explicitly stating the thresholds are project targets and not measured results from the original video.

nodes.label: Long-Level Reserve Requirement
nodes.rationale: A level may hold hundreds of logical items but only dozens of real rigid bodies at any moment, and reserve waves of complete triples must surface from the basket bottom rather than dropping in from the top of the screen.

nodes.label: Simulator QA Evidence Package
nodes.rationale: Records iOS Simulator and Android emulator evidence for fast iteration and mobile-browser regression catching, while explicitly not replacing the physical Device QA release gate.

nodes.label: Android Software-Renderer Compatibility Pile
nodes.rationale: The runtime classifies the Android Emulator OpenGL ES Translator automatically and switches to a real-asset DOM pile backed by authoritative game state; the hidden Three/Cannon loop pauses and resumes with a discarded clock delta so physics cannot jump. It proves rules, assets, layout and input only, never production WebGL, physics performance, audio, haptics or motion.

nodes.label: dist:digest Build Identity
nodes.rationale: Every simulator evidence package signs exactly one 214-file dist digest, so a geometry or asset change after the run invalidates the signature and forces a rerun.

nodes.label: Visible-Surface-First Pick Rule
nodes.rationale: Oversized invisible tap proxies could hit the ray before another item's real visible surface, so picking always prefers the nearest visible authored surface and falls back to hollow-item proxy volumes only when no real surface is hit.

nodes.label: Minimum Simulator Evidence Contract
nodes.rationale: Requires app version, dev URL, dist digest, all three theme IDs, iOS and Android screenshots, an explicit localhost bridge, WebGL canvas presence, fallback state, and a pick proof where trayCountAfter > trayCountBefore, so a static screenshot cannot pass.

nodes.label: public/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt Release Copy
nodes.rationale: The shipped public asset mirrors the repository notices so the CDN-delivered bundle carries the required runtime-library attributions and ISC/MIT license text.

nodes.label: Zhuada-e Design QA Matrix
nodes.rationale: Compares the reference frame and implementation screenshots at the same viewport to check composition, density, layering, controls, material and motion continuity; final result is conditionally passed with Android physical-device WebGL still open (P0:0, P1:1, P2:0).

nodes.label: Broad-Face Rest Physics Correction
nodes.rationale: Thin cards, wedges, paper parcels and shallow trays resting on edge collapse to a rectangle from the top-down camera and read as a mismatch with their tray thumbnail, so nearly sleeping thin bodies receive a bounded angular-velocity correction rather than a quaternion write or a locked orientation; collisions and Shake can still tip them.

nodes.label: v5 Material Finish Skin Pass
nodes.rationale: v2's uniform high-intensity bump made porcelain, glaze, produce and fabric look identically grainy, so successive passes moved to finish-specific responses and per-object skin phases with warm wood/paper fibre and cool glaze/metal highlights, never painted stripes or badges.

nodes.label: Farm-Kitchen Kettle Silhouette Rebuild
nodes.rationale: The old side-view handle collapsed into a black slash from the overhead camera and the upended body read as fruit, so the kettle gained a genuine three-dimensional bail spanning X/Z and arching in Y, a curved spout, a lid field and an enamel ring that stay readable upright, on its side and mid-roll.

nodes.label: Marker-Free Identity Expression Rule
nodes.rationale: Identity is carried by silhouette, whole-body colour block, proportion and material only; slashes, crosses, rings, badges, cords, stamps and thin banding were removed from both source atlases and runtime hint feedback, which instead lifts, scales and emissively pulses the object itself.

nodes.label: 1870ms Triple-Match Tray Choreography
nodes.rationale: Ordinary slotting/grouping uses a readable 750ms beat; a triple runs 240ms highlight, 420ms clear and 460ms left-compaction, with tray movement constrained to translate3d/opacity and 3D press, flight arc, camera kick and pan-toss timings centralised in scene-motion.ts to avoid scattered magic numbers.

nodes.label: Broad Hue-Family Colour Distribution
nodes.rationale: A fixed hue offset clustered unrelated items into purple/mint and let three large same-kind bodies clump, so treatments now distribute per product family, cover at least seven hue families per deal, cap single-bucket crowding, and scatter each opening triple across three pile sectors.

nodes.label: Zhuada-e HTML App Shell
nodes.rationale: Portrait mobile shell with viewport-fit=cover and apple-mobile-web-app meta, mounting src/main.tsx into #app and pointing icon/og:image at the generated logo.png and banner.png.

nodes.label: MiniAppTarotVrf Contract
nodes.rationale: Asynchronous Neo N3 Tarot draw contract, compiled and mock-E2E tested but not deployed; it is independent from the existing MiniAppTarot deployment and must not update that contract in place.

nodes.label: Morpheus Oracle Randomness Source
nodes.rationale: 32 bytes are requested from Morpheus and the contract never falls back to Runtime.GetRandom; on network magic 894710606 a null deploy payload selects the pinned canonical TESTNET Morpheus hash, and every other network must supply an explicit Oracle Hash160 with no cross-network default.

nodes.label: onOracleResult Callback Adapter
nodes.rationale: Used only when network magic is 894710606 and the configured Oracle is the canonical TESTNET contract 0x4b882e94ed766807c4fd728768f972e13008ad52.

nodes.label: onMiniAppResult Rich Callback Adapter
nodes.rationale: Every non-canonical-TESTNET deployment commits to the eight-argument adapter so settlement can bind caller, Oracle, network, app/module/operation, requester, reading and request IDs, player index, tombstone, adapter, fees, request time and a recomputed payload hash.

nodes.label: requestReading Entry Point
nodes.rationale: Takes (player, maxOracleFee); the live Oracle request fee is read at call time and bounded by both the player's maxOracleFee and the 0.1 GAS reading fee.

nodes.label: Rejection-Sampled Partial Fisher-Yates Card Draw
nodes.rationale: Derives three distinct cards in 0..77 from 32 oracle bytes; rejection sampling avoids the modulo bias a naive reduction would introduce.

nodes.label: Player Credit and Oracle Reserve Accounting
nodes.rationale: Two separate buckets with distinct memos (miniapp-tarot-vrf:credit in exact 0.1 GAS multiples, miniapp-tarot-vrf:oracle); successful readings split the fee between earned revenue and reserve replenishment.

nodes.label: Deadline Expiry Refund Convergence
nodes.rationale: Oracle failure, malformed entropy or local expiry restores the whole reading fee to withdrawable player credit while an already-spent Oracle fee stays an operator cost; after the deadline both transaction orderings converge, since a keeper can refund first and invalidate a later callback, or a callback arriving first performs the expiry refund instead of drawing cards.

nodes.label: vrf_random Semantics Caveat
nodes.rationale: vrf_random currently means signed Morpheus CSPRNG output and is explicitly not a formal proof-carrying VRF, so integrators do not over-claim verifiability.

nodes.label: build_tarot_vrf.sh Pinned Compiler Build
nodes.rationale: Pins Neo.Compiler.CSharp 3.9.1 and checked arithmetic so contract bytecode is reproducible.

nodes.label: verify_tarot_vrf_morpheus_testnet.mjs Read-Only Verifier
nodes.rationale: Verifies TESTNET network magic, canonical Oracle hash, ABI generation, method signatures/safety flags and the current request fee without loading a WIF or building a transaction.

nodes.label: Completed-Reading Read Surface
nodes.rationale: completedReadingsCount and playerCompletedReadingCount count successful spreads only, so pending and refunded requests are never presented to a client as cards drawn.
